drivingQuestion: Are the verses governing redemption of a sold ancestral field and of a Hebrew slave to be expounded as a leniency for the redeemer, and on what basis?
outcomeNote: The lenient reading stands: the field learns גאולה–גאולה from the Hebrew slave, Abaye turns back the argument from the slave׳s sinfulness with ׳הא אהדריה קרא׳, and Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak׳s reading of ׳בשנים׳ as the change in the slave׳s value survives the rival float and is endorsed by Rav Yosef as Sinaitic.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מְכָרָהּ לָרִאשׁוֹן בְּמָנֶה, וּמְכָרָהּ רִאשׁוֹן לַשֵּׁנִי בְּמָאתַיִם, מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְחַשֵּׁב אֶלָּא עִם הָרִאשׁוֹן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״[לָאִישׁ] אֲשֶׁר מָכַר לוֹ״.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «The Sages taught:» Consider the case where the owner of a field «sold it to the first» buyer «for one hundred» dinars «and the first» buyer then «sold it to the second» buyer «for two hundred» dinars. «From where» is it derived «that» when the original owner redeems the field, «he calculates» the payment «only» according to the price that he set «with the first» buyer? «The verse states:» “And he calculates the years of its sale, and he returns the remainder to the man «to whom he sold it”» (Leviticus 25:27).

segments.he: מְכָרָהּ לָרִאשׁוֹן בְּמָאתַיִם, וּמָכַר הָרִאשׁוֹן לַשֵּׁנִי בְּמָנֶה, מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין מְחַשְּׁבִין אֶלָּא עִם הַשֵּׁנִי? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״לָאִישׁ [לָאִישׁ] אֲשֶׁר בְּתוֹכוֹ״, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי.
segments.en: Now consider the case where the owner of a field «sold it to the first» buyer «for two hundred» dinars «and the first» buyer then «sold» it «to the second» buyer «for one hundred» dinars. «From where» is it derived «that» when the original owner redeems the field, the payment «is calculated only» according to the price that was paid «by the second» buyer? «The verse states:» “And he returns the remainder «to the man» to whom he sold it.” The superfluous term «“to the man”» indicates that the verse is referring to the man «who is» currently «in» possession of the field. This is «the statement of Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi.

segments.he: רַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מְכָרָהּ לוֹ בְּמָנֶה, וְהִשְׁבִּיחָהּ וְעָמְדָה עַל מָאתַיִם, מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְחַשֵּׁב אֶלָּא בְּמָנֶה? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְהֵשִׁיב אֶת הָעוֹדֵף״ — הָעוֹדֵף שֶׁבְּיָדוֹ.
segments.en: «Rabbi Dostai ben Yehuda says» that the verse should be interpreted differently: Consider the case where the owner of a field «sold it to» the buyer «for one hundred» dinars, «and» the field «appreciated» in value while in the buyer’s possession «and» its value «stood at two hundred» dinars. «From where» is it derived «that» when the seller redeems the field «he calculates» the payment «only» according «to» the «one hundred» dinars he originally received for the field?«As it is stated: “And he returns the remainder» to the man to whom he sold it,” that is, the seller returns only «the remainder» of the original payment «that is in his possession.»

segments.he: מְכָרָהּ לוֹ בְּמָאתַיִם, וְהִכְסִיפָה וְעָמְדָה עַל מָנֶה, מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין מְחַשְּׁבִין אֶלָּא בְּמָנֶה? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְהֵשִׁיב אֶת הָעוֹדֵף״ — הָעוֹדֵף שֶׁבַּקַּרְקַע.
segments.en: Rabbi Dostai ben Yehuda continues: Consider the case where the owner of a field «sold it to» the buyer «for two hundred» dinars, «and» the field «depreciated» in value while in the buyer’s possession «and» its value «stood at one hundred» dinars. «From where» is it derived «that» when the seller redeems the field, the payment «is calculated only» according «to» the «one hundred» dinars the field is currently worth? «As it is stated: “And he returns the remainder» to the man to whom he sold it,” i.e., he returns «that which» now «remains of the» value of the «land.»

segments.he: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ? דְּאִיַּיקַּר, וְזָל, וְאִיַּיקַּר.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «What is» the practical difference «between» the opinions of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi and Rabbi Dostai ben Yehuda? The Gemara responds: The practical difference between them is in a case «where» the field’s value «was high» at the time of the first sale, e.g., it was worth two hundred dinars, «and» when the field was sold a second time it had «depreciated» in value and was worth only one hundred dinars. «And» when the original owner came to redeem it, it again «appreciated» in value until it was worth two hundred dinars. According to Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, the redemption payment is calculated according to the one hundred dinars paid by the second buyer for the field. According to Rabbi Dostai ben Yehuda, it is calculated either according to the remainder of the original payment or according to that which now remains of the value of the land. Either way, it is calculated according to the remainder of two hundred dinars.

segments.he: וּמִמַּאי דִּלְקוּלָּא? דִּלְמָא לְחוּמְרָא!
segments.en: The aforementioned practical difference aside, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi and Rabbi Dostai ben Yehuda agree that the verses are interpreted in a manner that benefits the original owner. The Gemara asks: «And from where» is it derived «that» the verses should be interpreted «as a leniency» for the seller? «Perhaps» they should be interpreted «as a stringency» for the seller.

segments.he: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, דְּגָמַר ״גְּאוּלָּה״ ״גְּאוּלָּה״ מֵעֶבֶד עִבְרִי.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: Such a possibility should «not enter your mind, as it is learned» by means of a verbal analogy between the term «“redemption”» written in this context and «“redemption” from» the passage discussing «a Hebrew slave» that the Torah is lenient with regard to the redeemer. The verse states with regard to the redemption of a field: “And he prospers and finds sufficient means to redeem it” (Leviticus 25:26), and with regard to the redemption of a slave who was sold to a gentile, the verse states: “After he is sold he shall attain redemption” (Leviticus 25:48). Accordingly, just as the Torah is lenient with regard to the redemption of a Hebrew slave, so too the Torah is lenient with regard to redeeming a field.

segments.he: וְהָתָם מְנָלַן? דְּתַנְיָא: נִמְכַּר בְּמָנֶה, וְהִשְׁבִּיחַ וְעָמַד עַל מָאתַיִם, מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין מְחַשְּׁבִין אֶלָּא מִמָּנֶה? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״מִכֶּסֶף מִקְנָתוֹ״.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And there,» in the case of a Hebrew slave, «from where do we» derive that the Torah is lenient with regard to his redemption? The Gemara responds: «As it is taught» in a baraita: Consider the case of a Hebrew slave who «was sold for one hundred» dinars, «and he appreciated» in value during his term of servitude «and» his value «stood at two hundred» dinars. «From where» is it derived «that» if he redeems himself, the sum he pays for the remaining years of his service «is calculated only» according «to» the «one hundred» dinars for which he was originally sold? «As it is stated:» “If there are yet many years, according to them he shall return the price of his redemption «from the money of his purchase”» (Leviticus 25:51).

segments.he: נִמְכַּר בְּמָאתַיִם, וְהִכְסִיף וְעָמַד עַל מָנֶה, מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין מְחַשְּׁבִין אֶלָּא מִמָּנֶה? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כְּפִי שָׁנָיו״.
segments.en: The baraita continues: Consider the case of a Hebrew slave who «was sold for two hundred» dinars, «and he depreciated» in value during his term «and» his value «stood at one hundred» dinars. «From where» is it derived «that» if he redeems himself, the sum he pays for the remaining years of his service «is calculated only» according «to» the «one hundred» dinars he is currently worth? «As it is stated: “According to his years» he shall return the price of his redemption” (Leviticus 25:52). The verse indicates that the sum is calculated according to the value of his remaining years of service.

segments.he: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא עֶבֶד עִבְרִי הַנִּמְכָּר לְגוֹי, שֶׁנִּגְאָל וְיָדוֹ עַל הָעֶלְיוֹנָה, נִמְכָּר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״שָׂכִיר״ ״שָׂכִיר״ לִגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה.
segments.en: The baraita continues: «And I have» derived «only» with regard to «a Hebrew slave who was sold to a gentile, that he is redeemed and» that «he has the advantage,» as the price of his redemption is always calculated according to the lesser value. «From where» is it derived that this halakha also applies in the case of a Hebrew slave who was «sold to a Jew? The verse states: “Hired worker,” “hired worker,”» in order «to» derive «a verbal analogy,» indicating that this halakha applies both to a slave sold to a gentile and to one sold to a Jew. The verse states with regard to a slave sold to a gentile: “According to the time of a hired worker shall he be with him” (Leviticus 25:50), and with regard to a slave sold to a Jew, the verse states: “For double the hire of a hired worker he served you six years” (Deuteronomy 15:18).

segments.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי:
segments.en: The Gemara relates that «Abaye said:»

segments.he: הֲרֵינִי כְּבֶן עַזַּאי בְּשׁוּקֵי טְבֶרְיָא. אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מֵרַבָּנַן לְאַבָּיֵי: אִיכָּא לְמִידְרְשִׁינְהוּ לְקוּלָּא, וְאִיכָּא לְמִידְרְשִׁינְהוּ לְחוּמְרָא, מִמַּאי דִּלְקוּלָּא? אֵימָא לְחוּמְרָא!
segments.en: «I am» ready to answer any questions put to me «like» those of the intellectually sharp «ben Azzai,» who would regularly expound «in the markets of Tiberias. One of the Sages said to Abaye:» The verses discussing the redemption of a Hebrew slave «can be interpreted as a leniency» for the slave, «and they can» also «be interpreted as a stringency» for him. «From where» is it derived «that» the verses should be interpreted «as a leniency» for the slave? «Say» that they should be interpreted «as a stringency» for him.

segments.he: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּיךְ, מִדְּאַקֵּיל רַחֲמָנָא גַּבֵּיהּ, דְּתַנְיָא: ״כִּי טוֹב לוֹ עִמָּךְ״ — עִמָּךְ בַּמַּאֲכָל, עִמְּךָ בַּמִּשְׁתֶּה, שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא אוֹכֵל פַּת נְקִיָּה וְהוּא אוֹכֵל פַּת קִיבָּר, אַתָּה שׁוֹתֶה יַיִן יָשָׁן וְהוּא שׁוֹתֶה יַיִן חָדָשׁ, אַתָּה יָשֵׁן עַל גַּבֵּי מוֹכִין וְהוּא יָשֵׁן עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע; מִיכָּן אָמְרוּ: הַקּוֹנֶה עֶבֶד עִבְרִי כְּקוֹנֶה אָדוֹן לְעַצְמוֹ.
segments.en: Abaye explained: Such a possibility should «not enter your mind, due to» the fact «that the Merciful One was» explicitly «lenient with regard to» a slave. «As it is taught» in a baraita: The verse states with regard to a Hebrew slave: “And it shall be, if he says to you I will not leave «you…because he fares well with you”» (Deuteronomy 15:16). The term “with you” indicates that the slave must be «with you,» i.e., treated as your equal, «with regard to food,» and «with you with regard to drink.» This means «that you should not be eating fine bread» while «he eats inferior bread [kibbar],» bread from coarse flour mixed with bran. Likewise, «you» should not «drink old wine» while «he drinks» inferior «new wine. You» should not «sleep on» bedding made from «soft sheets» while «he sleeps on the ground. From here» the Sages «stated: One who acquires a Hebrew slave» is considered «like one who acquires a master for himself,» as he must ensure that the slave’s living conditions are equal to his own.

segments.he: אַדְּרַבָּה, נַחְמִיר עֲלֵיהּ מִדְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא! דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: ״בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה קָשֶׁה אֲבָקָהּ שֶׁל שְׁבִיעִית״.
segments.en: That Sage raised an objection to Abaye: «On the contrary, let us impose a stringency upon» the slave, «due to» the statement «of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina. As Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says» in explanation of the juxtaposition of several passages in the Torah (Leviticus, chapter 25): «Come and see how severe» is even «the hint of» violation of the prohibition of «the Sabbatical» Year, as the prohibition against engaging in commerce with produce of the Sabbatical Year is not one of the primary prohibitions of the Sabbatical Year, and yet its punishment is harsh.

segments.he: אָדָם נוֹשֵׂא וְנוֹתֵן בְּפֵירוֹת שְׁבִיעִית, לְסוֹף מוֹכֵר אֶת מִטַּלְטְלָיו, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״בִּשְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל הַזֹּאת תָּשׁוּבוּ אִישׁ אֶל אֲחוּזָּתוֹ״, וּכְתִיב: ״וְכִי תִמְכְּרוּ מִמְכָּר לַעֲמִיתֶךָ אוֹ קָנֹה מִיַּד עֲמִיתֶךָ״, דָּבָר הַנִּקְנֶה מִיָּד לְיָד.
segments.en: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, continues: If «a person has commercial dealings with produce» of the «Sabbatical» Year or of the Jubilee Year, «ultimately» he will become so poor that «he will» be compelled to «sell his movable property, as it is stated: “In this Jubilee Year you shall return every man to his possession”» (Leviticus 25:13), «and it is written» in the subsequent verse: «“And if you sell something to your neighbor or buy from your neighbor’s hand,”» which is referring to «an item acquired» by passing it «from hand to hand.» The juxtaposition of the two verses indicates that if one violates the halakhot of the Jubilee Year or the Sabbatical Year, he will eventually have to sell his movable property.

segments.he: לֹא הִרְגִּישׁ — לַסּוֹף מוֹכֵר אֶת שְׂדוֹתָיו, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְכִי יָמוּךְ אָחִיךָ וּמָכַר מֵאֲחֻזָּתוֹ״.
segments.en: If «he does not feel» remorse and he does not repent, «ultimately he will» be compelled to «sell his fields, as it is stated» in an adjacent verse: «“If your brother becomes poor and sells part of his ancestral land”» (Leviticus 25:25).

segments.he: לֹא בָּאת לְיָדוֹ — לַסּוֹף מוֹכֵר אֶת בֵּיתוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאִישׁ כִּי יִמְכּוֹר בֵּית מוֹשַׁב עִיר חוֹמָה״. מַאי שְׁנָא הָתָם דְּקָאָמַר ״לֹא הִרְגִּישׁ״, וּמַאי שְׁנָא הָכָא דְּקָאָמַר ״לֹא בָּאת לְיָדוֹ״? כִּדְרַב הוּנָא, דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא: כֵּיוָן שֶׁעָבַר אָדָם עֲבֵירָה וְשָׁנָה בָּהּ, הוּתְּרָה לוֹ.
segments.en: If consciousness of his sins «does not come to him, ultimately he will» be compelled to «sell his house, as it is stated: “And if a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city”» (Leviticus 25:29). The Gemara asks: «What is different there,» in the previous clause, «where» the tanna «says» that the sinner «does not sense» remorse, «and what is different here, where he says» that consciousness of his sins «does not come to him?» The Gemara responds: This is «in accordance with» the statement «of Rav Huna, as Rav Huna says: Once a person commits a transgression and repeats it, it is permitted to him.»

segments.he: הוּתְּרָה לוֹ סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ?! אֶלָּא אֵימָא: נַעֲשֵׂית לוֹ כְּהֶיתֵּר.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: Can it «enter your mind» to say that «it is» actually «permitted to him» because he has transgressed twice? «Rather, say» that «it becomes as» though it were «permitted to him,» that is, after transgressing the prohibition twice he becomes accustomed to this behavior and no longer feels that it is a sin. If one transgresses the prohibition only once, he is apt to feel remorse. Once he repeats his transgression, he loses this sensibility concerning his sins and will no longer feel any remorse.

segments.he: לֹא בָּאת לְיָדוֹ — לַסּוֹף שֶׁלֹּוֶה בְּרִבִּית, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְכִי יָמוּךְ אָחִיךָ וְגוֹ׳״, וּכְתִיב: ״אַל תִּקַּח מֵאִתּוֹ נֶשֶׁךְ וְתַרְבִּית״.
segments.en: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, continues: If consciousness of his sins «does not come to him, ultimately he» will be compelled to «borrow with interest, as it is stated: “And if your brother becomes poor» and his means fail with you, then you shall uphold him” (Leviticus 25:35), «and it is written» in the subsequent verse: «“You shall take no interest or increase from him.”»

segments.he: לֹא בָּאת לְיָדוֹ — עַד שֶׁמּוֹכֵר אֶת בִּתּוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְכִי יִמְכּוֹר אִישׁ [אֶת] בִּתּוֹ לְאָמָה״, וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּבִתּוֹ בְּהַאי עִנְיָנָא לֵיתַהּ, נִיחָא לְאִינִישׁ דְּלִיזַבֵּין בְּרַתֵּיה וְלָא לֵיזִיף בְּרִיבִּיתָא, דְּאִילּוּ הָתָם מְיגָרְעָא וְאָזְלָא, וְאִילּוּ הָכָא קָא מוֹסְפָא וְאָזְלָא.
segments.en: One «does not come to» borrow with interest «until he» has already been compelled to «sell his daughter, as it is stated: “And when a man sells his daughter as a maidservant”» (Exodus 21:7). The Gemara explains: «And even though his daughter is not» mentioned «in that context» in Leviticus, nevertheless, «a person prefers to sell his daughter and not to borrow» money «with interest.» This is «because there,» when one sells his daughter, the sum required in order to redeem her «continuously decreases, while here,» where one borrows with interest, his debt «continuously increases.» One may therefore assume that if one borrows with interest, he has already sold his daughter.

segments.he: לֹא בָּאת לְיָדוֹ — לַסּוֹף שֶׁמּוֹכֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי יָמוּךְ אָחִיךָ עִמָּךְ וְנִמְכַּר לָךְ״; לֹא לָךְ אֶלָּא לְגֵר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לְגֵר״, וְלֹא לְגֵר צֶדֶק אֶלָּא לְגֵר תּוֹשָׁב, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לְגֵר תּוֹשָׁב״.
segments.en: If consciousness of his sins «does not come to him, ultimately he will» be compelled «to sell himself, as it is stated: “And when your brother becomes poor with you and sells himself to you”» (Leviticus 25:39). «Not» only will he be sold «to you,» a born Jew; «rather,» he will even be sold «to a stranger, as it is stated:» “And sells himself «to the stranger”» (Leviticus 25:47). «And not» only «to» a stranger who is «a convert, but» even «to a gentile who resides in Eretz Yisrael and observes the seven Noahide mitzvot [ger toshav], as it is stated:» “And sells himself «to a ger toshav» with you” (Leviticus 25:47).

segments.he: ״מִשְׁפַּחַת גֵּר״ — זֶה הַגּוֹי. כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״אוֹ לְעֵקֶר מִשְׁפַּחַת גֵּר״ — זֶה הַנִּמְכָּר וְנַעֲשֶׂה מְשָׁרֵת לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה עַצְמָהּ.
segments.en: When the verse further states: “Or to the offshoot of «a stranger’s family,” this is» referring to «the gentile» relatives of a ger toshav, who are idolaters. «When it says: “Or to the offshoot [le’eker] of a stranger’s family,” this is» referring to «one who is sold and becomes a servant to idol worship itself,» i.e., he is put to work in a temple dedicated to idolatry. In any event, the baraita teaches that it is only due to an individual’s sins that he reaches such a low point that he must sell himself as a slave. If so, the verses dealing with a Hebrew slave should be interpreted in a stringent manner, so that the slave cannot easily be redeemed.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָא אַהְדְּרֵיהּ קְרָא, וְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: הוֹאִיל וְהָלַךְ וּמָכַר עַצְמוֹ לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, אֶידְחֶה אֶבֶן אַחֵר הַנּוֹפֵל? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״גְּאוּלַּת עוֹלָם תִּהְיֶה לּוֹ וּבַיּוֹבֵל יֵצֵא״. אֵימָא: גְּאוּלָּה תִּהְיֶה לוֹ — דְּלָא לִיטַּמַּע בַּגּוֹיִם, וּלְעוֹלָם לְעִנְיַן פִּדְיוֹנוֹ נַחְמִיר!
segments.en: Abaye «said to» that Sage: «But the verse» subsequently «restores him,» i.e., it requires that one strive to redeem him from slavery. As the tanna of «the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: Since he went and sold himself to» a temple dedicated to «idol worship, should I throw a stone after the fallen?» In other words, perhaps he should be left to his own devices? «The verse states: He shall have a perpetual right of redemption, and he shall leave in the Jubilee» (see Leviticus 25:31, 48). The Gemara objects: Even so, you can «say» that «he shall have a redemption» so «that he will not be assimilated among the gentiles, but actually, with regard to his redemption we will be stringent,» as it is due only to his sins that he is enslaved.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: כְּתִיב ״אִם עוֹד רַבּוֹת בַּשָּׁנִים״, וּכְתִיב ״אִם מְעַט נִשְׁאַר בַּשָּׁנִים״.
segments.en: «Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:» Two verses are written with regard to redeeming someone who was sold to a gentile. «It is written: “If there are yet many in the years,» according to them he shall return the price of his redemption from the money that he was bought for” (Leviticus 25:51). «And it is written» in the next verse: “And «if there remain but few in the years» until the Jubilee Year, then he shall reckon with him; according to his years he shall return the price of his redemption.”

segments.he: וְכִי יֵשׁ שָׁנִים מְרוּבּוֹת וְיֵשׁ שָׁנִים מוּעָטוֹת? אֶלָּא: נִתְרַבָּה כַּסְפּוֹ — ״מִכֶּסֶף מִקְנָתוֹ״, נִתְמַעֵט כַּסְפּוֹ — ״כְּפִי שָׁנָיו״.
segments.en: Now, «are there years with much» time «and years with little» time? Every year is the same length. «Rather,» this means that if «his monetary» value «appreciated» during the years of his service, he is redeemed according to «“the money that he was bought for,”» which is the lower sum. And if «his monetary» value «depreciated» over time, one determines his value «“according to his years,”» i.e., according to his current value rather than according to his previous worth. The verse indicates that one acts leniently when calculating the redemption payment of a Hebrew slave.

segments.he: וְאֵימָא: הֵיכָא דַּעֲבַד תַּרְתֵּי וּפָיְישִׁי אַרְבְּעֵי — לִיתֵּב לֵיהּ אַרְבַּע ״מִכֶּסֶף מִקְנָתוֹ״, וְהֵיכָא דַּעֲבַד אַרְבַּע וּפָיְישִׁי תַּרְתֵּי — לִיתֵּב לֵיהּ תַּרְתֵּי ״כְּפִי שָׁנָיו״!
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «But say» that the verses should be interpreted as follows: “If there are yet many in the years,” is referring to a case «where he served» for «two» years, «and four» years of servitude «remain.» In this situation «let him return to» his master the value of «four» years of his servitude according to «“the money that he was bought for.” And» the phrase “if there remain but few in the years” is referring to a case «where he served» for «four» years «and two» years of servitude «remain.» In this situation «let him return to» his master the value of «two» years of his servitude «“according to his years.”»

segments.he: אִם כֵּן, נִכְתּוֹב ״אִם עוֹד רַבּוֹת שָׁנִים״, מַאי ״בַּשָּׁנִים״? נִתְרַבָּה כַּסְפּוֹ בַּשָּׁנִים — מִ״כֶּסֶף מִקְנָתוֹ״, נִתְמַעֵט כַּסְפּוֹ בַּשָּׁנִים — ״כְּפִי שָׁנָיו״. אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: דַּרְשִׁינְהוּ רַב נַחְמָן לְהָנֵי קְרָאֵי כְּסִינַי.
segments.en: The Gemara rejects this suggestion: «If so, let» the verse «write: If there are yet many years. What» is the meaning of the phrase «“in the years”?» Rather, this indicates that if «his monetary» value «appreciated in the years» of his service, he is redeemed according to «“the money that he was bought for,”» which is the lower sum. If «his monetary» value «depreciated in the years,» one determines his value «“according to his years,”» i.e., according to his current value. Upon hearing this explanation, «Rav Yosef said: Rav Naḥman» bar Yitzḥak «interpreted these verses as» truly as if the interpretation had been transmitted to Moses from «Sinai.»

moves.summary: The Gemara opens with a baraita on reckoning the redemption of an ancestral field that the buyer resold.
moves.about: brings the baraita on how the redemption of a sold ancestral field is reckoned when the buyer resold it

moves.cueHe: מנין שאינו מחשב אלא עם הראשון?
moves.summary: Whence that a field sold for 100 and resold for 200 is reckoned with the first buyer?
moves.about: brings the redemption verse as the source for reckoning with the first buyer

moves.summary: Derived from ׳to the man to whom he sold it׳.
moves.about: ׳to the man to whom he sold it׳ fixes the reckoning on the price the first buyer paid, even when the field was resold dearer

moves.cueHe: מנין שאין מחשבין אלא עם השני?
moves.summary: The converse case: sold for 200, resold for 100.
moves.about: brings the same verse again for the converse case, where the field was resold cheaper

moves.summary: Derived from the superfluous ׳לאיש׳ — the man now holding it; these are Rabbi׳s words.
moves.about: the superfluous ׳לאיש׳ points to the man currently holding the field, so a cheaper resale lowers the reckoning

moves.summary: Rabbi Dostai reads the same verse of the field׳s appreciation: sold for 100 and risen to 200, he reckons by the 100 — the remainder in his hand.
moves.about: what ׳and he returns the remainder to the man to whom he sold it׳ measures — the price paid by whichever buyer holds the field, or the change in the field׳s own value

moves.summary: The converse: sold for 200 and fallen to 100 — the remainder in the land.
moves.about: brings the same phrase again for the case where the field depreciated

moves.summary: What practical case separates Rabbi from Rabbi Dostai?
moves.about: what practical case separates Rabbi׳s derivation from Rabbi Dostai ben Yehuda׳s

moves.summary: Where the field was dear, then cheap, then dear again.
moves.about: the two derivations part where the field was dear at the first sale, cheap at the second, and dear again at redemption

moves.summary: Whence that the verses are expounded leniently for the seller at all?
moves.about: on what basis both tannaim of the baraita read the verses as a leniency for the seller

moves.summary: Floats the stringent reading as the live alternative.
moves.about: perhaps the same verses should be expounded stringently against the seller rather than leniently

moves.summary: Knocks the floated stringency down: a גזירה שווה ׳גאולה׳–׳גאולה׳ from the Hebrew slave forces leniency.
moves.about: the stringent reading is impossible because the field׳s redemption learns its leniency from the Hebrew slave

moves.summary: And there, for the Hebrew slave, whence the leniency?
moves.about: whence the leniency in the redemption of a Hebrew slave, the source side of the verbal analogy just invoked

moves.summary: Cites a baraita on the self-redemption of a Hebrew slave.
moves.about: brings the baraita on reckoning the self-redemption of a Hebrew slave

moves.summary: Sold for 100 and appreciated to 200 — reckoned from the 100.
moves.about: brings ׳from the money of his purchase׳ as the source for capping the slave׳s redemption at his original lower price

moves.summary: Sold for 200 and depreciated to 100 — again the lesser sum.
moves.about: brings ׳according to his years׳ as the source for the converse case, where the slave depreciated

moves.cueHe: ואין לי אלא עבד עברי הנמכר לגוי
moves.summary: A שכיר–שכיר verbal analogy extends the leniency to a slave sold to a Jew.
moves.about: a שכיר–שכיר verbal analogy extends the lenient reckoning from a slave sold to a gentile to one sold to a Jew

moves.summary: Abaye declares himself ready for any question, like ben Azzai in the markets of Tiberias.
One of the Sages takes up the challenge: the verses can be read either way — whence the lenient reading?
moves.about: on what basis the Hebrew slave׳s redemption verses are expounded leniently rather than stringently, since both readings are open

moves.cueHe: לא סלקא דעתיך, מדאקיל רחמנא גביה
moves.summary: Abaye answers from the Torah׳s own leniency toward the slave — ׳כי טוב לו עמך׳, food, drink and bedding as his master׳s.
moves.about: the stringent reading is excluded because the Torah itself is explicitly lenient toward the Hebrew slave

moves.summary: On the contrary — R׳ Yosei son of R׳ Ḥanina׳s cascade shows enslavement is the end of a chain of sin, so be stringent.
moves.about: whether the slave should be treated stringently instead, since enslavement is the last stage of a chain of sin

moves.summary: The cascade begins: trading in Sabbatical produce ends in selling one׳s movable property.
moves.about: brings the Jubilee verse as the head of the juxtaposition proving the descent into poverty

moves.cueHe: לא הרגיש — לסוף מוכר את שדותיו
moves.summary: Then his fields.
moves.about: brings the verse on selling ancestral land as the next stage of the descent

moves.cueHe: לא באת לידו — לסוף מוכר את ביתו
moves.summary: Then his house.
moves.about: brings the verse on selling a house in a walled city as the next stage

moves.summary: Why ׳he did not sense it׳ in the one clause and ׳it did not come to him׳ in the next?
moves.about: why the exposition says ׳he did not sense it׳ in one clause and ׳it did not come to him׳ in the next

moves.summary: Per Rav Huna: once a man transgresses and repeats it, it becomes permitted to him.
moves.about: the change of wording tracks Rav Huna׳s rule that a repeated transgression stops registering as one

moves.summary: Can a transgression really become permitted?
moves.about: a transgression cannot literally become permitted merely because it was repeated

moves.summary: Emend Rav Huna: it becomes AS IF permitted to him — he stops feeling it as sin.
moves.about: Rav Huna׳s words are to be restated as ׳it becomes AS IF permitted to him׳

moves.cueHe: לא באת לידו — לסוף שלוה ברבית
moves.summary: The cascade resumes: he borrows at interest.
moves.about: brings the verse on the impoverished brother as the head of the borrowing-at-interest stage

moves.cueHe: לא באת לידו — עד שמוכר את בתו
moves.summary: Before that he has already sold his daughter.
moves.about: brings the verse on selling one׳s daughter as a maidservant

moves.cueHe: ואף על גב דבתו בהאי ענינא ליתה
moves.summary: Explains why the daughter׳s sale is listed though it is not in that passage: her redemption price shrinks, a debt only grows.
moves.about: why the daughter׳s sale belongs in the cascade although it is not in that Torah passage — a man prefers it to a debt that only grows

moves.cueHe: לא באת לידו — לסוף שמוכר את עצמו
moves.summary: At last he sells himself — to a Jew, to a stranger, to a ger toshav.
moves.about: brings the verse on selling oneself into slavery as the next stage

moves.summary: And lowest of all, sold as a servant to idolatry itself — so his enslavement is the fruit of his sins.
moves.about: the verse׳s successive phrases mark ever lower buyers, down to being sold as a servant to idolatry itself

moves.summary: Abaye replies that the verse itself restores him — one does not throw a stone after the fallen; he has a perpetual right of redemption.
moves.about: even after that descent the verse itself restores him, commanding a perpetual right of redemption, so leniency stands

moves.summary: Say the verse only keeps him from assimilating among gentiles, while his redemption price stays stringent.
moves.about: the verse may guarantee only that he not be assimilated among gentiles, while his redemption price is still reckoned stringently

moves.cueHe: אמר רב נחמן בר יצחק: כתיב ״אם עוד רבות בשנים״
moves.summary: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak sets the two redemption verses side by side.
moves.about: brings ׳if there are yet many in the years׳ as one half of the pair he will expound

moves.cueHe: וכי יש שנים מרובות ויש שנים מועטות?
moves.summary: Years are all equal — so the verses speak of value risen or fallen, and the Torah itself reckons leniently.
moves.about: ׳many in the years׳ means his monetary value grew, so he is redeemed by the original purchase money

moves.cueHe: ואימא: היכא דעבד תרתי ופיישי ארבעי
moves.summary: Floats a rival reading: the verses divide by how many years of service remain.
moves.about: the two verses might instead divide by how many years of service remain, not by any change in the slave׳s value

moves.cueHe: אם כן, נכתוב ״אם עוד רבות שנים״
moves.summary: Rejects the float — the verse would have written ׳many years׳, not ׳many IN the years׳.
moves.about: the floated reading that the verses divide by remaining years is dismissed on the strength of the wording ׳בשנים׳

moves.cueHe: אמר רב יוסף: דרשינהו רב נחמן להני קראי כסיני
moves.summary: Rav Yosef: Rav Naḥman expounded these verses as though they had been given so at Sinai.
moves.about: Rav Yosef commends Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak׳s exposition of these verses as though it had been given at Sinai
